ns1:channel.ns1:title: Nature Sustainability
ns1:channel.ns1:description: Nature Sustainability will publish significant original research from a broad range of natural, social and engineering fields about sustainability, its policy dimensions and possible solutions. Understanding how to ensure the well-being of current and future generations within the limits of the natural world is the overarching goal of sustainability research. Nature Sustainability will cover topics including water, air and soil pollution, agriculture and food security, water–energy–land nexus, water-soil-waste nexus and climate change, among many others.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Preparing for disasters
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01956-y

The impacts of extreme natural events are dramatic for both people and physical infrastructure. More can and should be done to contain the damage and prevent loss of life.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Restoration-driven positive and negative leakage in sub-Saharan Africa
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01936-2

Restoration initiatives are important for progress towards climate and biodiversity policy goals; however, whether they lead to the displacement of tree loss elsewhere (leakage effect) is still unclear. This study examines the leakage impacts of restoration projects in sub-Saharan Africa.
ns1:item.dc:title: Restoration-driven positive and negative leakage in sub-Saharan Africa
ns1:item.dc:creator: Xinran Miao

ns1:item.ns1:title: Navigating the land–energy nexus for carbon-neutral power systems in China
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 30 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01941-5

As countries expand renewable energy to reach net zero, finding suitable land is becoming increasingly challenging. A new China-wide optimization study shows that land constraints redirect renewable development, increase transmission needs and raise 2060 system costs by up to 4.1%.
ns1:item.dc:title: Navigating the land–energy nexus for carbon-neutral power systems in China
ns1:item.dc:creator: Ziheng Zhu
Runxin Yu
Da Zhang
